ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 3, unchanged since cycle 13 and re-affirmed rather than re-litigated. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 16 (attempts [16]); no source has been added and no candidate has changed status. The floor is firm: the primary claim rests on three unaffiliated teams (src-0002 CTIBench, src-0005 CyberSOCEval, src-0007 CyberThreat-Eval), and src-0007 supplies the within-table control that cross-benchmark synthesis cannot -- ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (GPT-4o FT) and 0.1771/0.1414 (GPT-4o-mini FT), against IoC-extraction precision of 0.8240-0.8846 for the SAME four models on the SAME corpus in the SAME table. Those nine figures have now been pulled verbatim TWICE (cycle 15's G2 to four decimal places, cycle 21's whole-table pull), which makes them the best-verified numbers in this knowledge base. WHY THAT IS STILL A 3. The level-4 bar is counterarguments explicitly ADDRESSED, and the binding one is unchanged and now in its ELEVENTH cycle of being merely listed: open_question[1] wants a human-analyst baseline F1 for ATT&CK technique extraction. Every number in this issue is an absolute score with no human reference point, so 'hard, unsolved sub-task' remains an interpretation of those numbers rather than a demonstrated comparison; adding sources that measure the same unanchored quantity makes it more reliable without anchoring it. Cycle 16 answered open_question[2] in the negative (fine-tuning makes this sub-task WORSE), and cycle 21's Table 4 pull extends that pattern to triage precision, but narrowing an open question is not addressing a counterargument. NEW THIS CYCLE, AND IT ARGUES AGAINST ANY RISE RATHER THAN FOR ONE: src-0017 (added cycle 21) establishes that src-0007's released IoC evaluator matches predictions to ground truth by TWO-DIRECTIONAL SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT rather than strict equality. No cycle has pulled the corresponding scoring rule for src-0007's ATT&CK task. If the TTP task is scored by exact technique-ID match while the IoC task is scored leniently, then part of the 0.82-versus-0.28 within-table spread is a scoring-rule artefact rather than a task-difficulty fact. That does not undermine the ABSOLUTE finding that these models reach ~0.28 precision and ~0.20 recall on ATT&CK mapping -- which is what this issue's primary claim actually asserts -- so the score does not fall. It does mean the within-table control is weaker than cycles 16 and 19 took it to be, and the cheapest available strengthening move for this issue is now to pull src-0007's per-task evaluation protocol from the src-0017 artefact. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED, DO NOT LET IT BE STRIPPED: src-0005's per-model numeric scores have never been captured in fifteen cycles (carry-forward [10], the oldest un-actioned collection task in the project); cycle 9's G2 confirmed its claims in substance but explicitly NOT verbatim, so one of the three legs remains the weakest-verified in the base. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.

ioc-extraction-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 2 AFTER A CYCLE THAT MOVED THE EVIDENCE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Cycle 21's T3 was the first work on this issue since cycle 9 (attempts now [9, 21]) and the cycle-22 queue entry correctly warned that the honest score could go either way. It stays at 2, and the reason is structural rather than a judgement about how impressive the new work was. THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT: level 3 requires the PRIMARY candidate to be supported by at least two INDEPENDENT sources. Candidate 1 (LANCE 97.6% overall F1 against the manually-validated 1,791-IoC PRISM benchmark) rests on src-0003 alone. Candidate 2 (vanilla-LLM IoC precision 0.8240 GPT-4o / 0.8503 o3-mini / 0.8846 GPT-4o-FT / 0.6944 GPT-4o-mini-FT over 1,310 expert-annotated IoCs from a production workflow) rests on src-0007 alone. Cycle 21's NEW supported candidate 4 -- that the METRIC confound cannot account for the src-0003/src-0007 gap -- cites [src-0003, src-0007, src-0017], but src-0017 is the SAME TEAM's artefact release for src-0007, and both src-0017's own index entry and candidate 4's own text say so in terms ('rests on ONE independent measurement plus arithmetic over src-0003's published figure, not on two independent measurements'). Three source ids on a candidate is not three independent sources. So the issue still has no candidate meeting the level-3 bar, which is the textbook definition of a 2. I ENDORSE THAT SELF-ASSESSMENT RATHER THAN OVERRIDING IT; a candidate that states its own independence limit honestly should be taken at its word, not scored as if it had not. WHAT CYCLE 21 GENUINELY ACHIEVED, RECORDED SO THE HELD SCORE IS NOT MISREAD AS NO PROGRESS. The metric confound is ELIMINATED, and that is the single largest advance this issue has had: cycle 18's arithmetic (reconciliation by metric artefact alone requires IoC recall of 0.09-0.15) plus a verbatim Section 4.3 sentence from src-0007 -- 'In the TI drafting stage, the extraction of IoCs is relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary' -- from a paper that calls the TTP task 'a substantial challenge' at recall 0.1414-0.2270. And src-0017 shows the released evaluator computes recall in the same function as precision and prints it on the next line, so the omission is a reporting decision, not a measurement limit. One open_question is largely answered, three are narrowed. This is a materially better 2 than cycle 19's. WHAT MY OWN G2 ADDED, AND IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY ON EVERY POINT. I re-verified src-0003 (last verified cycle 5, sixteen cycles, and the load-bearing never-replicated side of ctr-0001). Substance passed on every load-bearing figure -- 1,791 IoCs from 50 reports, 97.6% overall F1, >90% F1 across all types, 43% analyst time drop, >6% downstream F1 -- all returned verbatim, and the [31] quote-splice check PASSED on all three stored quotations. But three findings weaken this issue's comparison rather than strengthen it. (i) THE 97.6% IS A CLASSIFICATION SCORE OVER A REGEX-EXTRACTED CANDIDATE SET, not a free-form extraction score. Verbatim: 'We assume a total of 1,789 candidate indicators, extracted using IoC Searcher, a state-of-the-art rule-based tool'; 'LANCE labeled over 99% of all extracted indicators'; and Figure 9's caption reads '... on IoC Classification'. The LLM labels indicators a regex has already found. src-0007's 0.8240 is precision on IoCs a model produces itself from an article. That is a difference in TASK FORMAT, not merely in scaffolding -- and unlike the 'Vanilla LLMs' caption reading, which cycle 21 correctly downgraded to an inference the paper never states, this one is stated by the paper. It is the strongest textual anchor the SYSTEM confound has ever had, and it also makes the two numbers less commensurable than any cycle has recorded. (ii) SRC-0003 NEVER STATES ITS MATCHING RULE. A targeted verbatim search of its evaluation and methodology sections for 'exact match', 'matched', 'matching', 'normaliz', 'defang', 'case-insensitive', 'ground truth', 'true positive' and 'false positive' produced no sentence saying how a predicted indicator is compared with a ground-truth one. So the open_question cycle 21 added -- strict equality versus substring/normalised matching -- CANNOT BE CLOSED FROM THE SOURCES IN THIS BASE. It is not merely unresolved; it is unresolvable without a source we do not have. (iii) A PROVENANCE DEFECT IN THE STORED BASELINE FIGURES. The comparison values in src-0003's key claim ('IoC Searcher + whitelist 76% F1, AlienVault OTX 72% F1, VirusTotal threshold=1 86% F1') are NOT PRESENT AS TEXT anywhere on the page: the strings '76' and '72' do not occur, and the only '86%' is 'Its lowest score, 86.8% recall on domains ...', which is LANCE's own per-type recall. There is no table of per-tool performance; the numbers exist only inside Figure 6, an image this agent cannot read. The ORDERING is textually supported (VirusTotal at thresholds 1 and 5 are 'the two highest performing ground truth generation methods ... as indicated in Figure 6'; the whitelist method 'suffers from poor precision'; AlienVault 'yields the most unlabeled indicators (37%)'), so 86 > 76 > 72 is consistent with the prose and the substance is not falsified -- but these three numbers must be cited as figure-derived and not text-verified. This is the second source in the base found carrying an unverifiable stored 'reported' value, after src-0016's spliced quote (cycle-21 item [31]). I appended corrective key_claims to src-0003's index entry and an appendix to state/knowledge/src-0003.md rather than editing anything, so the correction lives in the knowledge base and not only in a log -- which is precisely how src-0016's defect survived six cycles. WHY I DID NOT OPEN A CONTRADICTION ENTRY FOR IT, stated so a successor can reverse me: G3's trigger, in prompts/system.md rule 3, is TWO SUPPORTED CLAIMS IN CONFLICT. There is no rival claim here asserting different baseline values, and I cannot read Figure 6, so I cannot assert 76/72/86 are wrong -- only that they are not text-verifiable. Filing a contradiction for an unverified-provenance finding would dilute the G3 signal, which is the mechanism the whole loop depends on. Cycle 21 reached the same conclusion on src-0016 and cycle 12 on ENISA's silence; I follow that precedent and record the defect as a documented verification gap instead. G3 GATE ARITHMETIC, STATED SEPARATELY SO IT IS AUDITABLE, AND THIS IS THE THIRTEENTH CYCLE THE DIVERGENCE HAS STAYED LATENT. Merit score on the evidence = 2. ctr-0001 (opened cycle 9, resolved_cycle null) is still the graph's only open contradiction and is filed against this issue, so the G3 gate applies. I applied the CEILING reading: score may not exceed scale_max minus g3_contradiction_demotion = 5 - 2 = 3. MERIT SCORE 2 AND CEILING-APPLIED SCORE 2 ARE THE SAME, SO THE CEILING DID NOT BIND. The cycle-21 handoff and cycle-20 before it both predicted the two readings would finally diverge here; they did not, because the honest merit score is still below the ceiling. Recorded explicitly per carry-forward [4] so a human sees that the divergence remains UNTESTED rather than resolved: the specification conflict is real and unfixed -- prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 and config.yml line 35's comment both say SUBTRACTION (which would give 0 here, stamping an issue that has four candidate_resolutions with the rubric label 'no candidate resolutions' and handing the weakest-link selector a fabricated bottom), while scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 ENFORCES A CEILING and would not even notice the subtraction. Cycle 16 ruled for the ceiling and wrote replacement text in logs/cycle-016.md 'Item 3'; prompts/, config.yml and scripts/ are outside this agent's output surface, so it awaits a human. Under subtraction this issue would now read 0 and would be selected forever. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY MOVE THIS SCORE: a second independent measurement of report-level IoC extraction, or a head-to-head. Of ctr-0001's three confounds, METRIC is now eliminated, SYSTEM has gained its first paper-stated anchor (task format) while losing its inferred one, and CORPUS is completely untouched and is now the largest gap in the issue -- nobody has compared PRISM's 50 public reports with src-0007's unnamed company's internal daily workflow for difficulty. Two further obstacles are independent of all three: src-0007's substring-containment matcher with a ground truth never stated to be exhaustive, and src-0003's unstated matching rule. ctr-0001 stays open and a T4 has no standing to close it.

consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode.rationale: HELD AT 2. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 16 (attempts [3, 15, 16]) and no source has been added, so this is a re-affirmation. THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT is unchanged: both SUPPORTED candidate_resolutions cite evidence [src-0001] and nothing else, and level 3 requires the primary candidate to rest on at least two independent sources. A second candidate that sharpens the first using the same source is not a second source. The four sources added at cycle 15 -- src-0013 (ECE/Brier calibration on secure code generation), src-0014 (prompt-sensitivity and abstention on vulnerability detection), src-0015 (action-threshold calibration for incident-response agents), src-0016 (same-input repeat-query stability on JavaScript SAST) -- are attached as candidate 3 at status 'proposed', and cycle 16's T2 made an explicit SCOPE RULING (candidate 4) declining to treat security-adjacent corroboration as CTI multi-source support. I ENDORSE THAT RULING rather than re-litigating it, for the reason cycle 19 gave and which is worth restating because it is the crux of this issue: every one of the four new sources measures a NON-CTI task, and this issue's whole content is that CTI reliability has axes beyond accuracy. Promoting on them would assert the very cross-domain generalisation the parent issue treats as an open question. So the DIRECTION of the phenomenon is corroborated four ways and the CTI-SPECIFIC claim is still single-source. That is exactly a 2. VERIFICATION STATE IS NOW UNUSUALLY GOOD FOR A 2, and it does not raise the score because verification quality is orthogonal to source count. All four cycle-15 sources have now been G2-verified (src-0013 c18, src-0014 c19, src-0015 c20, src-0016 c21), discharging carry-forward [20]. src-0014 has table-level confirmation of its body sentences by an independent route (its five stored coverage figures are exact arithmetic complements of Table 2's self-consistency abstention column to the second decimal; Table 3 reproduces all four recall-collapse pairs cell for cell). But src-0016's re-verification was NOT a clean pass: cycle 21 found that the stored 'verbatim' quotation about 80 of 161 unique-unmatched findings does not exist on the page as written -- it splices a real sentence to a table cell -- and that its collection note claiming no table was present is false (there are four). The figures are correct, so it is a quotation defect, and it is repaired by appendix. MY OWN G2 THIS CYCLE FOUND THE SAME DEFECT CLASS IN A SECOND SOURCE (src-0003's baseline F1 values are figure-image-only and not text-verifiable; see that issue's rationale). Two of two sources subjected to the exact-string check have now failed it in some respect, and neither had ever been checked that way before. That is a general finding about this knowledge base's provenance, and it bears on this issue specifically because src-0016 is one of the four sources under candidate 3: if candidate 3 were ever promoted, one of its legs would be a source with a known quotation defect. It does not lower the score -- candidate 3 is correctly 'proposed' and contributes nothing to the current 2 -- but it removes any argument that the four-source corroboration is a safe shortcut to 3. ALL FOUR open_questions remain wholly unaddressed. ONE OBSERVATION FROM CYCLE 19'S PULL THAT A FUTURE CYCLE CITING src-0014 MUST CARRY: Table 3's precision sits near 0.5 for every model under every prompting strategy (0.487-0.531 DeepSeek, 0.499-0.517 Mistral, 0.488-0.646 Gemma, 0.492-0.517 Falcon, 0.491-0.495 CodeLlama) on a binary task, which is a substantive limit on how much any of its F1 movement can mean. No open contradiction, so no G3 adjustment. SELECTOR NOTE, DERIVE IT YOURSELF RATHER THAN TRUSTING THIS: this issue is tied at 2 with ioc-extraction-reliability and automated-triage-under-refusal, and its attempts are [3, 15, 16]. Whether the cycle-15 and cycle-16 attempts still fall inside the five-cycle penalty window depends on the cycle the T5 actually runs on, and cycle 19's window arithmetic should not be copied forward.

attribution-confident-wrong-gap.rationale: HELD AT 3. The primary candidate rests on two genuinely independent sources of different kinds: src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-TAA over 50 real reports, where every one of five tested models' plausible-sounding attribution rate exceeds its correct rate -- GPT-4-turbo 86% plausible against 52% correct, Gemini-1.5 74% against 38%) and src-0004 (Heise reporting Der Spiegel on ENISA's APT29/Midnight Blizzard misattribution in an official report). An academic benchmark plus investigative reporting on a production incident is real independence and is what separates this issue from the single-source 2s. ONE OF CYCLE 19'S TWO RESERVATIONS ABOUT CANDIDATE 2 IS NOW DISCHARGED AND THE SCORE STILL DOES NOT MOVE, which is worth setting out because it is the kind of change that invites inflation. Candidate 2 carries src-0007's Table 4 'Content: Threat Actor' rubric block -- GPT-4o 1.547 Relevance / 1.528 Accuracy / 1.140 Attribution against o3-mini 3.964 / 3.656 / 2.968 on the same task, corpus and rubric, with the load-bearing element being the WITHIN-TABLE contrast rather than the model gap: the same GPT-4o scores 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.612 on 'Content: Root Cause' in the same table, so 1.140 on threat-actor attribution is a deficit specific to attribution rather than a general inability to draft. Cycle 19 declined to count it as a third leg for two reasons. Reason (2) -- that these values came from a single cycle-15 pull and had never been independently re-pulled -- is DISCHARGED: cycle 21 pulled Table 4 whole and verbatim and transcribed the full rubric block into state/knowledge/src-0007.md, discharging carry-forward [25], so the values no longer live only in logs/cycle-015.md and issue prose. Reason (1) is not merely undischarged but CONFIRMED AND HARDENED: the GPT-4o (FT) column reads 3.964 / 3.655 / 2.967 against o3-mini's 3.964 / 3.656 / 2.968, tracking to within 0.001 on all six rubric rows, and cycle 21's independent pull reproduced the cells identically. So it is as-printed rather than a fetch artefact, and the cause is unknown. Two independent pulls agreeing means the anomaly is real, not that it is explained -- any claim resting on that column must say the column is suspect. A third caution stands: the rubric's ABSOLUTE level is uninterpretable, since 1.140/5 normalises to 0.228 or 0.035 depending on x/5 versus (x-1)/4, a normalisation the paper never states, so only within-table contrasts may be cited. And in any case candidate 2's source, src-0007, is already in this issue's evidence list, so re-verifying it improves confidence in a leg that was already counted rather than adding a leg. NOT RAISED TO 4, unchanged reason, now in its NINTH cycle: open_question[2] asks whether src-0004's naming-convention hallucination is the same phenomenon as src-0002's quantified plausible-versus-correct gap or a distinct citation/naming-fabrication sub-type. That is the explicit alternative explanation for why these two sources sit in one issue and no cycle has argued it either way. Level 4 requires counterarguments ADDRESSED, not articulated, and this one is load-bearing: if the ENISA error is a citation-fabrication sub-type then this issue's second leg is really evidence for institutional-incident-real-world-impact and this issue is closer to single-source than it looks. Also unchanged and already true at cycles 7, 10, 13 and 19, so not scored down on again: the AI-causation of the ENISA leg rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise, and spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent (carry-forward [13]), so that leg cannot strengthen without a source we cannot currently reach. No open contradiction, so no G3 adjustment.

task-dependent-reliability-framing.rationale: LOWERED 4 -> 3. THIS IS THE ONLY SCORE THAT MOVES THIS CYCLE AND IT REVERSES CYCLE 19'S RAISE, so the reasoning is given in full and a successor should audit it hardest. IT MOVES BECAUSE NEW EVIDENCE CREATED A MATERIAL COUNTERARGUMENT THAT THE ISSUE DOES NOT ADDRESS AND DOES NOT EVEN ARTICULATE -- not because I read the same evidence less generously. Cycle 19 raised this issue to 4 on an explicit and well-argued ground: level 4 needs counterarguments addressed, the counterargument that could sink the issue is open_question[3] (would the task-dependence conclusion survive an independent replication showing a smaller IoC-extraction advantage, i.e. is the whole pattern an artefact of leaning on src-0003's single-study never-replicated LANCE result), and the answer is that it survives with src-0003 removed entirely because the two strongest legs are WITHIN-STUDY designs that hold team, corpus, models and harness constant and vary only the sub-task -- src-0007 (IoC precision 0.8240-0.8846 against ATT&CK 0.2787/0.2270 and 0.3480/0.1759, plus 1.140/5 attribution against 3.612/5 root-cause in the same rubric) and src-0006 (one corpus, one 15-model set, nine sub-tasks all in F1, true range 0.286-0.882). That argument was correct on the evidence available at cycle 19. It has a hole that only became visible afterwards. THE COUNTERARGUMENT: A WITHIN-STUDY DESIGN HOLDS TEAM, CORPUS, MODELS AND HARNESS CONSTANT BUT DOES NOT HOLD THE SCORING RULE CONSTANT, and cross-sub-task score spreads are only task-difficulty facts if the sub-tasks are scored comparably. Two findings that post-date cycle 19 turn this from a quibble into a live objection. (a) src-0017 (added cycle 21) establishes that src-0007's released IoC evaluator matches predictions to ground truth by TWO-DIRECTIONAL SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT rather than strict equality, and that its README never states the ground truth is exhaustive per article. The corresponding rule for src-0007's ATT&CK task has never been pulled. If IoC extraction is scored leniently and ATT&CK technique identification by exact ID match, some unknown part of the roughly 3x within-table spread is a scoring-leniency artefact. (b) My own G2 on src-0003 this cycle found, verbatim, that its 97.6% is a CLASSIFICATION score over a regex-extracted candidate set -- 'We assume a total of 1,789 candidate indicators, extracted using IoC Searcher'; 'LANCE labeled over 99% of all extracted indicators'; Figure 9's caption '... on IoC Classification' -- so src-0003's leg of candidate 1 compares a closed-set labelling score with open-ended generation scores. That is a task-FORMAT difference, not only a sub-task difference. WHY THIS BITES LEVEL 4 SPECIFICALLY. It does not touch the level-3 bar, which is comfortably cleared: two supported candidates rest on seven distinct sources from at least five unaffiliated teams (candidate 1 [src-0001, src-0002, src-0003, src-0005, src-0006], candidate 2 [src-0007, src-0013]), and the qualitative claim that measured CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task is not in doubt. It bites level 4 because level 4 is about counterarguments being ADDRESSED, and this one is not stated anywhere in the issue, in either candidate, or in any open_question. An issue cannot be credited with addressing an objection it has not noticed. NOT ALL LEGS ARE AFFECTED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A 3 AND NOT A 2. src-0007's rubric contrast (Threat Actor 1.140 against Root Cause 3.612) is measured on ONE instrument, so it is immune to the matching-rule objection, and it alone establishes a large within-study cross-sub-task spread. src-0006's nine rows are all F1 on one corpus and model set, so the statistic is constant even though the per-task definition of a correct answer has never been pulled and could differ. The claim therefore remains supported; it is the ROBUSTNESS that fails. WHAT RESTORES 4, stated concretely so this is not a dead end: pull src-0007's per-task evaluation protocols from the src-0017 artefact (the IoC evaluator is already read; the TTP and rubric scorers are not), and src-0006's per-task scoring definitions, then state and answer the objection in the issue. If the scoring rules turn out comparable, cycle 19's argument stands as written and the 4 is correct. I ALSO CONSIDERED AND REJECTED CYCLE 19'S OWN STATED CASE FOR 3 AS MY GROUND. Cycle 19 recorded that a successor could drop this to 3 on the view that candidate 2 supplies the material answering open_question[3] without ever CROSS-REFERENCING it in the state. I do not rely on that; I think cycle 19 was right that a candidate whose entire stated point is source-independence IS an address rather than a raw ingredient. I am demoting on the substantive ground above, which cycle 19 could not have known. That distinction matters for the paper: this is a score responding to new evidence, not to a re-reading. WHAT I CONSIDERED AS A COUNTERARGUMENT AND CONCLUDED IS NOT ONE, carried forward from cycle 19 because the reasoning is still right: cycle 18's derivation that src-0006's mean between-MODEL range within a task (0.272) equals the mean between-TASK range within a model (0.263) to within 0.009 does NOT undercut this issue. A mean between-task range of 0.263 within a single model, running to 0.404 for LL70, directly CONFIRMS that reliability varies sharply by sub-task. What it undercuts is the claim that sub-task is the PRIVILEGED explanatory variable, which lives in the child issue extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis. Carry-forward [23] reached the same conclusion. RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES CARRIED, DO NOT LET THEM BE STRIPPED: src-0013's leg of candidate 2 measures secure code generation, not CTI, and correctly defers to the cycle-16 scope ruling; src-0005 has never had a numeric value captured in the entire project (carry-forward [10]); candidate 1's prose still contains superseded ordinal-axis language that the cycle-16 split moved out of this issue, and a future T2 or T3 should annotate rather than delete it; and src-0003's stored baseline comparison figures (76/72/86) are figure-image-only per my G2 and must not be cited as reported values. Three open_questions remain, so 5 was never in view. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment.

extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis.rationale: HELD AT 3, on the same reasoning cycle 19 gave when it first scored this issue, and I re-checked the load-bearing parts rather than taking them on trust. Nothing has touched the issue since cycle 18 (attempts [17, 18]). SCORED ON EVIDENTIAL STATE, NOT ON THE POLARITY OF THE ANSWER: the title question is answered in the NEGATIVE -- the ordinal ranking is not supported -- and a supported negative answer is a supported resolution, since the rubric is definitional about whether a supported resolution exists rather than about what it concludes. The primary candidate is supported by two independent sources from unaffiliated teams on different corpora with disjoint model sets, by two distinct routes. Route 1, src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows: Contextualization stage mean 0.636 against Attribution stage mean 0.602, a gap of 0.034 that is in the predicted direction but is roughly one eighth of the 0.272 mean between-model spread on a single task, and the best-performing task in the whole subset is TTP Extraction at 0.673, an Attribution-stage task -- so the ordering is not merely weak, it is locally INVERTED at its strongest predicted point. Route 2, src-0007's Table 4, the source that appears to support the ordering, reverses its own middle-to-third rung between two models of the same family under both defensible normalisations. WHY THE NEW MATCHING-RULE FINDING DOES NOT LOWER THIS SCORE, EVEN THOUGH IT LOWERED task-dependent-reliability-framing. src-0017's substring-containment finding and my own G2 finding that src-0003's headline is a classification score both undermine confidence that cross-sub-task numbers are commensurable. For the PARENT issue that is adverse, because the parent's supported claim asserts a real cross-sub-task difference. Here it is neutral-to-favourable, because this issue's supported claim is EVIDENTIAL and NEGATIVE: that the available commensurable measurement does not support the proposed ordering. If the measurements are less commensurable than believed, then there is even less evidence supporting the ordering. I checked the reverse reading -- that route 1 is weakened because the 'commensurable measurement' it rests on may not be commensurable -- and it does not change the outcome: under that reading no commensurable measurement supporting the ordering exists either, so the negative claim survives both ways. What it does add is a THIRD unaddressed caveat, which keeps this issue well away from 4. WHY 3 AND NOT 4. Level 4 needs counterarguments addressed and the candidate states four material caveats of which only one is addressed. (a) src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so the headline 0.034 carries NO uncertainty estimate -- stated, not addressed, and not addressable from any source in this base. (b) Four of the nine rows are strictly monotone decreasing across all eight general-purpose model columns in exactly the printed order (carry-forward [22], reproduced three times); this one IS addressed, by a robustness check dropping all four, leaving 0.641 against 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, same best task. (c) THE DECISIVE ONE: the fourth rung of the proposed ordering, open-ended GENERATION, is not represented in the commensurable subset at all, so the candidate refutes only part of a four-rung ordering and is SILENT on one quarter of the ordering named in this issue's own title. (d) NEW THIS CYCLE: per-task scoring rules within src-0006's nine F1 rows have never been pulled, so 'all in F1' establishes that the statistic is constant, not that the matching rules behind it are. Seven open_questions remain, two of them fundamental. WHY NOT 2, since the standing instruction is to take the lower score when torn. I resolved to 3 on the same ground cycle 19 did: for a claim whose content is explicitly evidential, showing that the strongest apparent supporting source self-destructs on its own table is direct evidence for that claim rather than mere absence of evidence. The honest case for 2 is that route 2 is DEFEATING rather than CONFIRMING evidence, which would leave src-0006 alone carrying the claim and make it single-source. A successor that takes that view should drop it to 2 and say so; my reason for not doing so is that the local inversion (TTP Extraction at 0.673 beating every Contextualization task) is a qualitative fact about a printed table and does not depend on the missing uncertainty estimate. THE THIRD CANDIDATE IS CORRECTLY 'proposed' AND CONTRIBUTES NOTHING: model identity as the replacement explanatory variable, resting on the between-model 0.272 versus between-task 0.263 near-equality, which cycle 18 itself objects to on three grounds (ranges are not variance components and are outlier-sensitive, the cross-source TTP comparison behind its corpus-identity limb is uncontrolled in at least four ways at once, and both figures come from one study's table). Its src-0014 limb was re-verified verbatim at cycle 19 and is exact; that confirms the citation, not the hypothesis. No open contradiction, so no G3 adjustment.

institutional-incident-real-world-impact.rationale: HELD AT 3. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 12 (attempts [12]); no source has been added and no candidate has changed status, so this is a re-affirmation and the cycle-13 reasoning that raised it from 2 to 3 stands unamended. The existence claim is carried by candidate 2 with evidence [src-0009, src-0010, src-0004]: ENISA's OWN publication pages carrying verbatim revision notices against publication dates of 1 October 2025 and 6 November 2025, both revised 09 January 2026, corroborating report count, dates, defect type and correction date independently of the Der Spiegel/Heise chain that was previously the entire basis. And by candidate 3 with evidence [src-0012, src-0004]: a second named incident at a different institution type (EY Canada, 16 of 27 references hallucinated per GPTZero, report withdrawn), discovered by the identical route of an outside party clicking through footnotes. Two incidents at two institutions via two mutually independent investigations, plus the affected institution's own correction record, clears the level-3 bar. NOT RAISED TO 4, and the two reasons are unchanged and both structural. (a) THE BASE RATE IS UNMEASURED AND IS BLOCKED BY SCOPE, NOT BY EVIDENCE VOLUME. Two named incidents are two data points, not a rate, and open_question[0] asks for a rate across CTI publishers. src-0011 (GhostCite) is not that rate and its candidate is correctly 'proposed': it audits peer-reviewed conference papers, which have reviewers where CTI reports have none; it defines a ghost citation as one absent from any major academic database, largely inapplicable to CTI footnotes which are news and vendor URLs; it reports per-PAPER rates (1.01% of Security-venue papers containing at least one invalid citation) not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492; and its own authors call it a conservative lower bound. Treating a second anecdote plus an adjacent-population audit as a resolved base rate remains the most likely error available on this issue and it is not being made. Note also carry-forward [18]: src-0011 contradicts itself in prose versus table (body text says NeurIPS exhibits 'the highest absolute count (391 papers)' while Table 3 gives 391 invalid citations across 308 papers), so any cycle quoting its counts must take them from Table 3's columns. (b) THE AI-CAUSATION LEG IS THE WEAKEST PART AND IT IS THE PART THE TOPIC IS ABOUT. For ENISA, AI attribution rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise (src-0004); ENISA's own pages assign no cause at all, spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent (carry-forward [13]), and every outlet repeating the 26-of-492 figure cites Der Spiegel, which is repetition rather than corroboration. For EY the 72% AI figure is the output of GPTZero's own commercial AI-detection product, so the load-bearing element there is the manually-checkable citation count. What is robustly established is that FABRICATED CITATIONS reached production at two named institutions; that AI CAUSED them is well-supported for EY and reported-but-not-primary for ENISA. A PERMANENT LIMIT RATHER THAN A PENDING ITEM, per carry-forward [14]: the two ENISA v1.2 PDFs cannot be opened by this agent at all (no PDF text extraction exists on this runner), so 'ENISA never disclosed the AI use' is established at landing-page level and is UNVERIFIABLE at document level here. That leg cannot strengthen and no further budget should be spent on it. Three of five open_questions remain wholly or mostly open, and candidate 4 itself honestly concludes there is no single institutional response pattern to report -- an accurate non-answer on n=2, not a resolution. NO G3 ADJUSTMENT: no contradiction is filed against this issue, and cycle 12's reasoning for not opening one over ENISA's silence is endorsed -- the revision notices assign no cause at all, and silence is not a competing claim, so G3's 'two supported claims in conflict' is not met. That is the same test I applied this cycle in declining to file a contradiction over src-0003's unverifiable baseline figures, and the consistency is deliberate. Best available route to a 4 remains carry-forward [16]: GPTZero runs an automated pipeline over the right population and publishes findings one report at a time, the only lead any cycle has found that could produce a rate rather than another anecdote.

automated-triage-under-refusal.rationale: HELD AT 2, AND ONE OF CYCLE 19'S TWO REASONS FOR THE 2 IS NOW DISCHARGED. This issue still has attempts [] -- it is the only issue in the graph never worked on -- but cycle 21's Table 4 pull gave it evidence as a by-product, discharging carry-forward [19]. THE FORMAL READING WOULD STILL GIVE 3 AND IT IS STILL WRONG. The single candidate_resolution is at status 'supported' with evidence [src-0007, src-0015], which on a mechanical count is two independent sources on the primary candidate. The state itself forbids that count: src-0015's own index entry records it as THE WEAKEST-PROVENANCE SOURCE IN THIS BASE and says in terms that it must not be the sole support for any candidate_resolution -- single-author preprint filed cs.AI with no stated venue, peer review or affiliation; n = 40 synthetic RL-seed episodes per model from a 60-seed pool with no confidence intervals, so only the GPT-5.2-versus-Sonnet-4.5 contrast is robust and the middle two models' ordering is unresolved. The candidate itself agrees, stating that the claim RESTS on src-0007 and that src-0015 'is worth little as independent quantification'. Two sources of very unequal quality must not read as two independent confirmations, so what this issue has is one load-bearing source plus a directional corroborator: a 2 by the rubric's definition of partial evidencing. That reason is UNCHANGED. WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS A REAL IMPROVEMENT: cycle 19's SECOND reason was that the one figure this issue's score rests on -- src-0007's triage precision/recall asymmetry -- had never been through a verbatim table pull, resting instead on collection-time summary. Cycle 21 pulled Table 4 whole and verbatim, and the stored '0.27-0.40 versus 0.90-1.00' HOLDS AS STATED: across both triage tasks and all four models, precision (Accepted) spans 0.2717-0.3982 and recall (Accepted) spans 0.9091-1.0000. So this is now a table-verified 2 rather than a summary-derived one, which is exactly the kind of quiet strengthening the loop is supposed to produce. NEW FROM THE SAME PULL, and it sharpens the issue's content rather than its score: fine-tuning does not fix the asymmetry and on the Article task WORSENS precision (GPT-4o 0.3037 -> GPT-4o FT 0.2717 with recall unchanged at 0.9798-1.0000), the same direction as src-0001's fine-tuning finding and cycle 16's ATT&CK finding. A THIRD, UNENTERED OBSERVATION BEARS ON THE CENTRAL OPEN QUESTION AND SHOULD BE USED BY WHOEVER WORKS THIS ISSUE: src-0015's Table 1 has a Reward column no cycle has recorded (GPT-5.2 3.07, Sonnet 4.5 2.37, Gemini 3 2.61, DeepSeek 3.2 3.45), so THE MODEL THE PAPER CALLS BEST-CALIBRATED EARNS THE LOWEST REWARD and the two highest-containment models take the two highest rewards. That points at the harness rather than the models, which is precisely what open_questions[0] asks. It is an observation about an already-collected source, so no new citation is needed to use it -- but its caveats travel with it: the fetched material does not state the reward's composition, n = 40 per model with no CIs, and the association is not strictly monotone (DeepSeek outscores GPT-5.2 at lower containment). Carry-forward [27]. THE DECISIVE REASON THIS IS NOT 3 REMAINS: the issue's title question is not answered by its own supported candidate. open_questions[0] asks whether over-acceptance is a property of the MODELS or of the HARNESS, and neither source varies the decision threshold, the stated cost of a false positive, the availability of an explicit abstain option, or the presence of a human confirmation step. The issue text concedes that until that experiment is run, 'the models under-refuse' and 'these harnesses were built with no refusal affordance' are INDISTINGUISHABLE -- and src-0003 already established for a different sub-task that scaffolding can dominate measured reliability, a point my G2 this cycle strengthened by showing src-0003's 97.6% is a classification score over a regex-extracted candidate set rather than a free-form extraction score. So the harness explanation is not hypothetical, it is the live rival. All five open_questions are unaddressed, including whether any precision-recall frontier exists (nobody has published the precision these models reach at a recall of 0.7, so it is unknown whether this is a tuning problem or a capability problem) and what the operational cost actually is (src-0007's ground truth IS the human analyst's accept/reject decision, so by construction it carries no human error bar and cannot say whether human triage would score better on its own benchmark). REMAINING VERIFICATION GAP, STATED HONESTLY: src-0015 was G2-verified at cycle 20 and PASSED with strengthening, so cycle 19's complaint that it had never been verified is also discharged -- but its index URL is an /abs page, which carries no tables, and the recovered columns came from a later pull. WHAT IS STILL ENTIRELY MISSING is the curl/HackerOne case (carry-forward [15]) -- the bug bounty ended 31 January 2026 after a flood of AI-generated reports, with roughly 20% of submissions AI slop by mid-2025 and the confirmed-vulnerability rate falling from about 15% to under 5%. It is currently an open_question on this issue and NOT evidence: no curl source exists in state/knowledge/index.json and G1 forbids inventing one. Cycle 19 judged it the highest-value uncollected source in the project and I agree; per carry-forward [29] a T3 may add sources, so a T3 targeting this issue is the first realistic route to it in many cycles. One pooling error to avoid, recorded at the candidate and repeated here: src-0015's 'calibration' is an action-threshold construct (false-positive rate, evidence-gating), NOT the ECE/Brier confidence calibration of src-0001 and src-0013, and the two must never be averaged or quoted as one measurement. No open contradiction, so no G3 adjustment.
